French

[edit]
French Wikipedia has an article on:
espion
Wikipedia fr

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Middle French *espion (attested only in the verb espionner), from Old French espion, spion (“one assigned to observe or spy”). Alternatively, derived from Old French espie (“spy”), under influence of Italian spione (“spy”).[1] According to another theory, French espion is borrowed from Italian spione.[2]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɛs.pjɔ̃/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
  • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)

Noun

[edit]

espion m (plural espions, feminine espionne)

  1. (espionage) spy (person who secretly watches)

  • → Turkish: ispiyon
